title: Django 6.x Native Background Tasks Architecture & Result Backend Contracts

claims.assertion: Background task execution subsystems must decouple task definition decorators from pluggable backend engines (immediate, DB, Redis) with standardized TaskResult lifecycle state machines

context: Traditional web frameworks rely on heavy external third-party task queues (Celery, Dramatiq) with inconsistent configuration semantics, impeding lightweight background execution and unit testability.
distilled_learning: Django 6.0 introduces a standardized `django.tasks` subsystem featuring `@task(queue='default', priority=1)` decorators returning executable `Task` objects. Tasks accept keyword arguments and return `TaskResult` futures with standard status transitions: `PENDING` -> `RUNNING` -> `SUCCESS` | `FAILED`. Pluggable task backends (`ImmediateBackend`, `DatabaseBackend`, `RedisBackend`) allow synchronous execution in test suites and distributed async queues in production without changing application task definitions.
